name: Moped
description: A motor vehicle with a rider's saddle and no more than three wheels on the ground that can't reach more than 30 mph within a mile, with a motor of no more than 5 brake horsepower (about 3,750 W). An electric bike over the electric bicycle's 750 watts or 28 mph, or without operable pedals, lands here while it stays within these limits.

restrictions.rule: A rider's saddle and no more than three wheels on the ground
Can't reach more than 30 mph within a mile, and its motor produces no more than 5 brake horsepower (about 3,750 W); the 50 cc and no-shift limits apply only to a combustion engine
Needs a driver's license but not a motorcycle (Class M) license, which covers motorcycles as defined, a term that excludes mopeds
Riders and passengers must wear a motorcycle helmet, unless 21 or older and either trained in an approved motorcycle safety course or covered by health insurance for motorcycle crash injuries
Registered with the Texas DMV for $30 a year, and must carry liability insurance
No faster than 35 mph at night unless its headlamp lights a person or vehicle 300 feet ahead
Carries a passenger only if built for one, with footrests and handholds, and never one under 5 except in a sidecar
Follows the rules for bicycles where they can apply, such as keeping near the right edge when slower than traffic
One that can go faster than 30 mph or has a motor over 5 brake horsepower is a motorcycle
